newsitem.title: KUWAIT: KOC starts 35,000 bpd production from neutral zone.
newsitem.headline: KOC starts 35,000 bpd production from neutral zone.

text.p: The production of some 35,000 barrels per day (bpd) of heavy crude started this month from the Neutral Zone between Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, industry executives said on Tuesday.
"The production started in the first two weeks of December and is running at 35,000 bpd," said one source familiar with a plan launched in 1991 to rehabilitate wells in al-Wafra field.

Production from the area is shared by Saudi Arabian Texaco, a unit of Texaco Inc, and Kuwait Oil Co (KOC). Executives said Kuwait's share was mainly being refined domestically by Kuwait National Petroleum Co.

"The rehabilitation plan over the past 18 months involved gathering centres and some 160 of the main wells," said one source. "Many wells and gathering centres were damaged during the (1990-91) Iraqi occupation" of Kuwait.
He could not give an exact estimate of costs but said at least $6 million have been spent so far on rehabilitation in Wafra with plans for additional work on other fields and gathering centres.

Kuwaiti officials were quoted in October as saying that Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Saudi Arabian Texaco had agreed to spend $400 million to raise output from onshore fields in the Neutral Zone to 300,000 bpd by 1998 from a current 190,000-200,000 bpd.
Japan's Arabian Oil Co Ltd operates off-shore fields in the zone and plans to raise output to 350,000 bpd by the end of the century from a current 315,000 bpd.
A majority of AOC stock is held by Japanese interests but Kuwait and Riyadh each hold a 10 percent stake in the firm.
Kuwait and Riyadh have equally shared the mineral rights to the zone since its establishment in 1922 by the sultanate of Nejd, now part of Saudi Arabia, and Kuwait, then a British protectorate.
